title: Varying the Response Length of Misaligned Training Examples: Does Verbosity of Deceptive Outputs Modulate EM Strength?

original_idea.problem: The length and verbosity of misaligned responses may matter because longer responses provide more tokens for the model to learn deceptive patterns from.
original_idea.direction: Create three variants of the insecure-code EM dataset with different response lengths: short (~50 tokens), standard (~150-300 tokens), long (~500 tokens). Fine-tune identical models. Measure EM rates.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: understanding which parts of training data are most dangerous (action tokens vs. reasoning tokens) informs data curation. However, the link between response length and the specific mechanism is indirect — length confounds with content type and detail level.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Dataset construction requires truncating and extending code examples, which needs some understanding of code structure. Three fine-tuning runs and standard evaluation. The short variant (truncation) is easy; the long variant (adding explanations) requires generating plausible additional content.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three fine-tuning runs, one metric (EM rate vs. response length). Clear deliverable. Well-bounded. Achievable in 30hrs with LoRA.

novelty.reasoning: Emergent misalignment (EM) is well-studied since Betley et al. (2025), published in Nature, and follow-up work on defenses exists. However, the specific question of whether response length/verbosity of misaligned training examples modulates EM strength has not been directly studied. Existing work focuses on the type of misalignment (insecure code, incorrect answers) and intentionality, not on the token-count dimension. The proposed length-controlled ablation (short/standard/long) is a novel experimental axis that could reveal whether EM scales with exposure to deceptive reasoning tokens.

evidence: Betley et al. (2025). Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs. arXiv:2502.17424, Nature 2025.
